sentences.text:
Facts of the case in brief is that the appellant/claimant was Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23218 driving the Tata ACE vehicle bearing No. CG 07 CA 1259 of the owner Khemlal Dewangan had gone to village Dughli (Maalighora) on 03.03.2013 for unloading the goods and while returning, though the vehicle was driven by him with moderate speed, at about 9.00 pm near vilage Pairi and Sikosa,
the offending vehicle Mahindra Tractor bearing registration No. CG07-NA/4132 and Trolley No.
CG07NA/4133 driven rashly and negligently by the respondent No.1 driver dashed the vehicle of the appellant/claimant causing severe injuries to him.
It was further pleaded that the appellant/claimant received fracture on his right leg and right hand.
He was taken to the hospital at Gunderdehi and looking to the seriousness of his injuries he was admitted in the hospital at Durg from 04.03.2013 to 15.04.2013.
His right leg and hand were operated and a rod was inserted and he is still undergoing the treatment.
It is stated that on account of the injuries sustained by him he is unable to drive the vehicle and have become permanently disabled.

The incident was reported to the police station Gunderdehi upon which Crime No. 36/2013 was registered and offence under Sections 279, 337 and 338 IPC was registered against the respondent No.1/driver Aafter due investigation charge sheet was filed before the JMFC Gunderdehi.
At the time of accident, the appellant/claimant was aged about 27 years and was earning Rs. 6,000/- per month working as a driver.
Since he has become permanently disabled, compensation of Rs. 32,66,000/- was claimed against the driver, owner and Insurance company of the offending vehicle.

3. Respondent No.1 and 2 driver and owner of the vehicle, filed their written statement and denied the averments of the claim application and pleaded that the appellant/claimant was rash and Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23218 negligent in driving his vehicle which dashed the offending vehicle therefore the offending vehicle got damaged.

It was further pleaded that the offending vehicle was driven by a license holder driver respondent No.1 and was insured with the Insurance Company/respondent No.3 therefore the liability to pay the compensation is upon the respondent No.3/Insurance Company.
4. Respondent No.3/Insurance Company filed its written statement and denied the averments of the claim application.
They also denied the pleadings with regard to permanent disability and also pleaded that the respondent No.1/driver was not negligent in causing the accident.
The respondent No.1/driver was holding valid and effective driving licence therefore the Insurance Company/respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation.
5. On the basis of the above broad pleadings, the learned Tribunal framed as many as 6 issues.
Issue with regard to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent No.1 driver was held to be proved.
Issue No. 2 with regard to sustaining severe injuries in the accident was held to be proved as appellant/claimant has suffered grievous injuries.
Issue No.3 was with regard to contributory negligence and the learned Tribunal found the contributory negligence to the tune of 50%.
Issue No.5 was with regard to violation of the Insurance Policy which was decided as not proved.

Issue No.4 & 6 was with regard to relief and cost and Rs. 2,33,650/- was awarded as compensation.
6.

Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that the learned Tribunal has committed an error of law in holding that the appellant/claimant was responsible for compensation to the tune of Dashrath Dhimar Nishad vs Devkumar Sahu on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136465324/

sentences.text: Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23218 50% as contributory negligence in causing the accident.
He further submits that looking to the evidence, 100% loss of earning should have been assessed by the learned Tribunal.
He further submits that the compensation awarded under the other heads is also on the lower side.
The income of the deceased was taken to Rs. 5,000/- which is on the lower side as he was earning Rs. 6,000/- per month.

7. Shri Patankar supported the award impugned and submits that the finding of the learned Tribunal is based upon proper appreciation of evidence and cannot be said to be contrary or perverse to the record and therefore needs no interference by this Court.
8. Heard counsel for the parties considered the rival submissions and also perused the records.
9. Appellant/claimant examined himself and AW-2 Dr. Deshmukh.

From The statement of the appellant/claimant, it appears that he was working as a driver and though he has stated that he was earning Rs. 6000/- but no cogent and prudent document to that effect has been filed therefore the learned Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the appellant/claimant to Rs. 5,000/- which in the opinion of the Court, looking to the date of accident cannot be said to be on the lower side.

10. The submission with regard to 100% loss of earning capacity is liable to be rejected on the basis of the evidence of the doctor and the documents appended (the disability certificate) with the claim application.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to accept the submission of loss of 100% earning capacity.
The finding with regard Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23218 to 50% negligence on the part of appellant/claimant appears to be perverse.

The driver and owner of the offending vehicle did not appear before the learned Tribunal to contest that the claimant/appellant was negligent rather from the statement of AW-1/appellant-claimant and the criminal papers appended and exhibited in the Tribunal, the negligence of the offending vehicle is established therefore this finding is set aside.
